{{Tooltip|W|Won}} 69–63 vs. [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]] }} {{2025-26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball standings}} The '''2025–26 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Michigan]] during the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. It was the program's 110th season and 109th consecutive year as a member of the [[Big Ten Conference]]. The Wolverines were led by second-year head coach [[Dusty May]] and played their home games at [[Crisler Center]] in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]]. On December 8, Michigan achieved the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings#USA Today Coaches Poll|No. 1 ranking in the Coaches poll]] for the first time since the [[Fab Five (University of Michigan)|Fab Five]]-led [[1992–93 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1992–93 Wolverines]], and on February 16, Michigan earned the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings#AP poll|No. 1 ranking in the AP poll]] for the first time since the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 Wolverines]]. On February 24, Michigan clinched a share of the [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2026 Big Ten regular season]] championship against [[2025–26 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]], and secured the outright Big Ten championship against [[2025–26 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|Illinois]] on February 27. It was the Wolverines' first since the [[2020–21 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2021 Big Ten regular season]] championship. Michigan finished the regular season 29–2, and 19–1 in the conference. Their 29 regular-season wins are a program record, and their 19 conference wins are a Big Ten record. The conference wins surpassed the previous program record of 16 wins by the [[1976–77 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1976–77]] and [[1984–85 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1984–85 Wolverines]], and surpassed the previous Big Ten record set by the [[1974–75 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|1974–75]] and [[1975–76 Indiana Hoosiers men's basketball team|1975–76 Indiana Hoosiers]] (18–0). Michigan is the only Big Ten team to have ever won all ten conference road games, and the first to finish undefeated on the road since the 1975–76 Hoosiers. It was also the first Michigan team to defeat [[Michigan–Ohio State men's basketball rivalry|rival]] [[Ohio State Buckeyes men's basketball|Ohio State]] three times in the same season. In the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2026 NCAA tournament]], Michigan made the Sweet Sixteen for an NCAA-leading ninth time in the last thirteen NCAA tournaments and set a program-record (and tied the [[2004–05 Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball team|2004–05 Illinois Fighting Illini]] for the Big Ten record) for single-season wins, 37, as they won the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship]] against [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]]. Michigan surpassed the previous single-season wins record of 33 by [[John Beilein]] and the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Wolverines]]. They became the first team to score at least 90 points in five games in a single NCAA tournament, and held their last four opponents to season-lows in [[field goal percentage]]. It was the second national title in program history and the first since [[1989 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1989]]. Michigan also became the first Big Ten team to win the national title since their rival [[1999–2000 Michigan State Spartans men's basketball team|Michigan State]] in [[2000 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2000]]. Michigan's dominance throughout the season led to a Big Ten single-season record +713 point differential. Following the season, May left the program to become the head coach of the [[Dallas Mavericks]].{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/basketball/2026/06/this-wasnt-an-easy-decision-dusty-may-explains-michigan-departure.html|website=[[MLive.com]]|date=June 23, 2026|title=‘This wasn’t an easy decision’: Dusty May explains Michigan departure|author=Zuke, Ryan}}{{cite web |title=Dallas Mavericks Name Dusty May Head Coach |url=https://www.nba.com/mavs/news/dallas-mavericks-name-dusty-may-head-coach |website=[[NBA.com]] |date=June 23, 2026}} ==Previous season== The [[2024–25 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Wolverines]] finished the [[2024–25 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2024–25 season]] with a 27–10 record, 14–6 in [[2024–25 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|conference play]] to finish the regular season tied for second place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2025 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|Big Ten tournament]], they defeated [[2024–25 Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball team|Purdue]] in the quarterfinal, [[2024–25 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]] in the semifinal, and [[2024–25 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] in the final, winning their first Big Ten tournament championship since [[2018 Big Ten men's basketball tournament|2018]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/3/16/mens-basketball-michigan-wins-2025-big-ten-tournament-championship-over-wisconsin |title=U-M Downs No. 18 Wisconsin to Capture B1G Tournament Title |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Matthew |last=Mahoney |date=March 16, 2025 |access-date=March 29, 2025}} The Wolverines received the Big Ten's automatic bid to the [[2025 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 5 seed in the South Region, where they defeated [[2024–25 UC San Diego Tritons men's basketball team|UC San Diego]], and [[2024–25 Texas A&M Aggies men's basketball team|Texas A&M]] to advance to their sixth Sweet Sixteen in the last eight NCAA tournaments. season== ===November=== ====Oakland==== On November 3, Michigan began the season with a 121–78 victory over [[2025–26 Oakland Golden Grizzlies men's basketball team|Oakland]], winning a 23rd consecutive season-opening game.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/11/michigan-sets-a-program-record-in-season-opening-blowout-of-oakland.html |title=Michigan sets a program record in season-opening blowout of Oakland |website=[[Mlive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 3, 2025}} For the first time in program history, seven Wolverines scored in double figures. Michigan was led by [[Morez Johnson Jr.]] with a career-high 24 points, while [[Aday Mara]] had 12 points, 12 rebounds and five blocks; his first double-double of the season. Five others scored in double figures, including freshman [[Trey McKenney]] scoring 21 points in his collegiate debut on 6-of-8 three-point shooting, [[Will Tschetter]] with 16 points, [[Nimari Burnett]] with 14 points, [[Yaxel Lendeborg]] added 12 points, and [[Roddy Gayle Jr.]] had 11 points. [[Elliot Cadeau]] added a career-high 14 assists in his debut.{{cite web|url=https://www.freep.com/story/sports/college/university-michigan/wolverines/2025/11/03/michigan-wolverines-basketball-oakland-golden-grizzlies-season-opener/87076278007/ |title=Michigan basketball shoots the lights out in 121-78 season-opening win over Oakland |newspaper=[[Detroit Free Press]] |first=Tony |last=Garcia |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 3, 2025}} Michigan scored a program-record 69 points in the first half, shooting 71% from the field and surpassing the previous record of 66 points set by the [[1987–88 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1987–88 Wolverines]] against [[Eastern Michigan Eagles men's basketball|Eastern Michigan]]. The 121 points were the most scored since the [[1989–90 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1989–90 Wolverines]] scored 127 against [[1989–90 Iowa Hawkeyes men's basketball team|Iowa]], and marked the sixth time in program history eclipsing 120 points in a game.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/4/mens-basketball-wolverines-set-scoring-records-in-opening-night-win-over-oakland |title=Wolverines Set Scoring Records in Opening Night Win Over Oakland |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Patrick |last=Ogrin |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 3, 2025}} The Wolverines finished shooting 64% from the field, tied a program-record with 19 made three-point shots (on 35 attempts: 54%), committed only eight turnovers, and had 55 bench points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401826083 |title=No. 7 Michigan scores school-record 69 points in 1st half, finishes with 121-78 win over Oakland |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 3, 2025 |access-date=November 3, 2025}} ====Wake Forest==== On November 11, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 Wake Forest Demon Deacons men's basketball team|Wake Forest]], 85–84 in overtime, during the Deacon-Wolverine Challenge at [[Little Caesars Arena]]. Michigan was led by Mara with 18 points, and career-highs 13 rebounds, six assists, and five blocks; his second double-double of the season. Cadeau had 17 points, a career-high eight rebounds, and seven assists, surpassing 200 career rebounds and 400 career assists. Gayle Jr. had 13 points, and Johnson Jr. added ten points and eight rebounds. With 13 rebounds, Mara surpassed 200 for his career.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/11/mens-basketball-wolverines-hang-on-for-overtime-victory-against-wake-forest-in-detroit |title=Wolverines Hang on for Overtime Victory Against Wake Forest in Detroit |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Patrick |last=Ogrin |date=November 11, 2025 |access-date=November 11, 2025}} Michigan led by 13 at halftime, but started 0-for-12 on three-point attempts in the second half, allowing Wake Forest to tie the game and force overtime. Cadeau scored or assisted on all five of Michigan's overtime points.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401817529 |title=No. 6 Michigan holds off Wake Forest 85-84 in overtime, led by Elliot Cadeau and Aday Mara |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 11, 2025 |access-date=November 11, 2025}} ====TCU==== On November 14, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 TCU Horned Frogs men's basketball team|TCU]], 67–63. Michigan was led by double-double performances from Lendeborg with 14 points and ten rebounds, and Johnson Jr. with ten points and 12 rebounds. McKenney scored 11 points and Gayle Jr. added ten points and six assists. With his ten rebounds, Lendeborg surpassed 800 in his NCAA Division I career.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/14/mens-basketball-wolverines-use-second-half-rally-to-top-tcu |title=Wolverines Use Second-Half Rally to Top TCU |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=November 14, 2025 |access-date=November 14, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401812252 |title=Transfers Yaxel Lendeborg and Morez Johnson Jr. have double-doubles as No. 6 Michigan wins at TCU |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 14, 2025 |access-date=November 14, 2025}} ====Middle Tennessee==== On November 19, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 Middle Tennessee Blue Raiders men's basketball team|Middle Tennessee]], 86–61. Michigan was led by Lendeborg with a game-high 25 points, and 12 rebounds, his second double-double of the season. Mara added ten points and ten rebounds off the bench, for his third double-double of the season, while Cadeau scored ten points. Tschetter added five points in his first start since March 13, 2024. Ten Wolverines scored during the game, with a season-high 13 players earning minutes. Michigan's defense forced 15 turnovers, the most by a Wolverines opponent in a game this season.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/19/mens-basketball-dominant-second-half-powers-u-m-past-middle-tennessee-to-fourth-straight-win |title=Dominant Second Half Powers U-M Past Middle Tennessee, to Fourth Straight Win |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=November 19, 2025 |access-date=November 19, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401822996 |title=Lendeborg scores 25, No. 7 Michigan tunes up for Las Vegas tourney by beating Middle Tennessee |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 19, 2025 |access-date=November 19, 2025}} ====San Diego State==== On November 24, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 San Diego State Aztecs men's basketball team|San Diego State]], 94–54, in the first game of the [[2025 Players Era Festival]]. Michigan was led by Lendeborg with a game-high 15 points, six rebounds and four assists. Five others scored in double figures, Johnson Jr. and Cadeau with 13 points each, Burnett and Gayle Jr. scored 11 points each, and Tschetter added ten points. Tschetter became the 76th Wolverine in program history to appear in 100 career games.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/25/mens-basketball-michigan-overpowers-san-diego-state-in-players-era-opener |title=Michigan Overpowers San Diego State in Players Era Opener |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Quinn |last=Schmidt |date=November 24, 2025 |access-date=November 24, 2025}} ====Auburn==== On November 25, Michigan defeated No. 21 [[2025–26 Auburn Tigers men's basketball team|Auburn]], 102–72, to advance to the Players Era Festival championship game. Michigan was led by Lendeborg with 17 points, five rebounds and four assists, while Gayle Jr. added a season-high 17 points and six rebounds. Four others scored in double figures, Burnett and Johnson Jr. with 15 points each, McKenney scored 11 points and Cason added ten points. Michigan used a 21–4 run late in the first half to extend their lead to 29 points. Michigan shot 51.5% from the field, including 14 of 35 (40%) from three-point range.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401823479 |title=No. 7 Michigan routs No. 21 Auburn 102-72 in Players Era Championship |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 25, 2025 |access-date=November 25, 2025}} A season-high 11 players reached the scoresheet, including freshman Winters Grady scoring his first career points. The win marked Michigan's first NCAA-recognized 30-plus-point win over a power-four opponent since a 104–68 win against No. 3 [[Purdue Boilermakers men's basketball|Purdue]] on March 3, 1987. The Wolverines scored 100-plus points against a ranked opponent for the first time since defeating No. 6 [[1989–90 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] 113–108 on December 9, 1989.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/25/mens-basketball-wolverines-dominate-21-auburn-in-players-era-blowout |title=Wolverines Dominate No. 21 Auburn to Advance to Players Era Championship |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Quinn |last=Schmidt |date=November 25, 2025 |access-date=November 25, 2025}} ====Gonzaga==== On November 26, Michigan defeated No. 12 [[2025–26 Gonzaga Bulldogs men's basketball team|Gonzaga]], 101–61, to win the Players Era Festival championship. Michigan was led by Lendeborg with a game-high 20 points and 11 rebounds, his third double-double of the season, and was named tournament MVP. Four others scored in double figures, McKenney with 17 points, Burnett scored 14 points, Mara had 13 points, and Johnson Jr. added 11 points. Cadeau recorded 13 assists, tied for the seventh most in a single game in program history.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/11/27/mens-basketball-michigan-cruises-past-no-12-gonzaga-to-claim-players-era-title |title=Michigan Cruises Past No. 12 Gonzaga to Claim Players Era Title |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Quinn |last=Schmidt |date=November 27, 2025 |access-date=November 27, 2025}} The Wolverines won their three games by an average of 36.7 points. Michigan's 40 point win was [[Mark Few]]'s worst loss in 902 games as Gonzaga's head coach, and the Bulldogs worst loss since losing 144–100 to [[Loyola Marymount Lions men's basketball|Loyola Marymount]] in 1990. Gonzaga was held to 33.8% shooting from the floor, including 3-of-22 (13.6%) from three-point range.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401831214 |title=No. 7 Michigan dominates No. 12 Gonzaga 101-61 to win Players Era Championship |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=November 27, 2025 |access-date=November 27, 2025}} The win marked the highest margin of victory against an AP ranked opponent in program history, and was the first time in NCAA history that any team outscored AP ranked opponents by 30 or more points in consecutive games.{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/11/the-best-team-in-the-nation-michigan-basketball-makes-its-case-for-no-1.html |title='The best team in the nation': Michigan basketball makes its case for No. 1 |website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=November 27, 2025 |access-date=November 27, 2025}} ===December=== ====Rutgers==== On December 6, Michigan opened the [[2025–26 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|Big Ten Conference season]] against [[2025–26 Rutgers Scarlet Knights men's basketball team|Rutgers]], defeating the Scarlet Knights, 101–60. Michigan was led by Johnson Jr. with a game-high 22 points. Five others scored in double figures, Lendeborg with 14 points, McKenney added 13 points, and Cadeau, Cason and Gayle Jr. scored 11 points each. Michigan shot 60% from the field and scored 22 of their first 24 points in the paint, and finished the game with a season-high 52 points in the paint.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401825400 |title=Johnson scores 22 as No. 3 Michigan routs Rutgers 101-60 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 6, 2025 |access-date=December 6, 2025}} The Wolverines scored more than 100 points for the third consecutive game, marking the first time this has occurred since the season they won the [[1989 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship in 1989]]. Michigan's 41-point win was the fourth-largest margin of victory against a Big Ten team in program history.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/12/6/mens-basketball-wolverines-rout-scarlet-knights-in-big-ten-opener |title=Wolverines Rout Scarlet Knights in Big Ten Opener |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Quinn |last=Schmidt |date=December 6, 2025 |access-date=December 6, 2025}} On December 8, Michigan achieved the [[2025–26 NCAA Division I men's basketball rankings#USA Today Coaches Poll|No. 1 ranking in the Coaches poll]] for the first time since the [[Fab Five (University of Michigan)|Fab Five]]-led [[1992–93 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|1992–93 Wolverines]], and No. 2 in the AP poll after an 8–0 start to the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2025/12/08/college-basketball-poll-rankings-top-25-michigan/87663337007/ |title=College basketball rankings get shakeup with Michigan new No. 1 in USA TODAY Sports poll |website=[[USA Today]] |first=Eddie |last=Timanus |date=December 8, 2025 |access-date=December 8, 2025}}{{cite web|url=https://www.mlive.com/wolverines/2025/12/michigan-basketball-one-step-closer-to-top-spot-in-ap-poll.html |title=Michigan basketball one step closer to top spot in AP poll |website=[[MLive.com]] |first=Andrew |last=Kahn |date=December 8, 2025 |access-date=December 8, 2025}} ====Villanova==== On December 9, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 Villanova Wildcats men's basketball team|Villanova]], 89–61. Michigan was led by Cadeau with 18 points, four assists and three rebounds. Mara added 11 points eight rebounds and two blocks, and McKenney scored ten points. The Wolverines went on an early 18–3 run, including scoring 15 straight points, in the first half and finished the half on a 12–0 run, to take a 30-point lead at halftime. Michigan's defense held Villanova to season lows in points (61), field-goal percentage (34 percent), and assists (six), while forcing a season-high 15 turnovers.{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2025/12/9/mens-basketball-cadeau-ignites-michigan-in-triumph-over-villanova |title=Cadeau Ignites Michigan in Triumph Over Villanova |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Quinn |last=Schmidt |date=December 9, 2025 |access-date=December 9, 2025}} Michigan became the only team since at least the [[1995–96 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|1995–96 season]] to win six straight games by at least 25 points with at least two of those victories against ranked opponents.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401823566 |title=No. 2 Michigan routs Villanova 89-61, remaining unbeaten with 6th straight win by 25-plus points |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=December 9, 2025 |access-date=December 9, 2025}} ====Maryland==== On December 13, Michigan defeated [[2025–26 Maryland Terrapins men's basketball team|Maryland]], 101–83. Michigan was led by Lendeborg with 29 points, a career-high nine assists, eight rebounds, three blocks and two steals, nearly posting a triple-double. Mara scored 18 points, Cason had a season-high 12 points, and Cadeau added 12 points and ten assists for a double-double. Maryland lost their leading scorer, [[Pharrel Payne]], with 4:36 remaining in the first half. Michigan trailed 45–50 at halftime, and overcame a halftime deficit for the second time this season and the first since they beat TCU on November 14. An early second-half nine-point deficit was the largest of the season to date. Michigan committed a season-low nine turnovers. The victory marked Michigan's 34th of the season, setting the single-season program record for wins, surpassing the previous record of 33 set by the [[2017–18 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2017–18 Wolverines]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/27/mens-basketball-u-m-defeats-no-18-alabama-to-set-program-win-record-advance-to-elite-eight |title=U-M Defeats No. 18 Alabama to Set Program Win Record, Advance to Elite Eight |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=March 27, 2026|access-date=March 27, 2026}} ====Elite Eight==== On March 29, Michigan defeated 6-seed No. 23 [[2025–26 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]], 95–62, in the largest margin of victory by any team in a regional final since the [[1988–89 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Wolverines]] in [[1989 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1989]]. As well as the second-largest margin of victory in program-history in any round, behind only that team. It was the worst loss by Tennessee in an NCAA tournament game and tied for the worst loss of [[Rick Barnes]]' career.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/michigan-tennessee-live-updates-march-madness-2026-elite-eight-score-results/live/|title=Michigan cruises into Final Four: Wolverines trounce Tennessee in Elite 8, set up showdown with Arizona|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|first=Isaac |last=Trotter|date=March 29, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}} Michigan was led by Lendeborg with 27 points and seven rebounds. Four others scored in double figures: Johnson Jr. and McKenney each had 12 points, Mara scored 11 points, and Burnett had 10 points. Cadeau added 10 assists, and became the first Big Ten player to record at least seven assists in four consecutive NCAA tournament games since [[Trey Burke]] in [[2013 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2013]]. Cadeau joined Lendeborg and Gayle Jr. on the Midwest All-Region team.{{cite web|url=https://www.si.com/college/michigan/basketball/three-michigan-basketball-players-on-midwest-all-region-team-after-elite-8-victory |title=Three Michigan Basketball Players on Midwest All-Region Team After Elite 8 Victory |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |first=Trent |last=Knoop |date=March 29, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48341285/michigan-overwhelms-tennessee-reach-1st-final-four-2018 |title=Michigan overwhelms Tennessee to reach 1st Final Four since 2018 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Adam |last=Rittenberg |date=March 29, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}} After an evenly scored start to the game, Michigan went on 34–10 run to close the first half, including a 21–0 run from eleven minutes until six minutes remaining, to lead 48–26 at halftime. The Wolverines continued expanding their lead to start the second half, going up 30 points with 14 minutes remaining as they cruised to their 35th win of the season and first Final Four since [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018]]. They held Tennessee to a season-low 19% field goal percentage. It was Michigan's fourth time defeating an AP ranked opponent by 30 points this season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap/_/gameId/401856576 |title=Yaxel Lendeborg scores 27 points as Michigan rolls into the Final Four, beating Tennessee 95-62 |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=March 29, 2026 |access-date=March 29, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/29/mens-basketball-michigan-advances-to-final-four-with-victory-over-tennessee |title=Michigan Trounces Vols to Punch Ticket to Final Four |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=March 29, 2026|access-date=March 29, 2026}} ====Final Four==== On April 4, Michigan defeated 1-seed No. 2 [[2025–26 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]], 91–73, to advance to the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game|national championship game]] for the first time since [[2018 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2018]].{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/4/4/mens-basketball-michigan-takes-down-arizona-advances-to-ncaa-tournament-title-game |title=Michigan Takes Down Arizona, Advances to NCAA Tournament Title Game |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=April 4, 2026|access-date=April 4, 2026}} Michigan was led by Mara with a career-high 26 points, nine rebounds, three assists, and two blocks. Four others scored in double figures: McKenney had 16 points on four three-pointers, Cadeau had 13 points, 10 assists, five rebounds and four steals, Lendeborg scored 11 points in 14 minutes, and Johnson Jr. added 10 points. Cadeau recorded the program's first point-assist double-double in the NCAA tournament since [[Derrick Walton Jr.]] in [[2017 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|2017]]. The Wolverines opened the game on a 10–1 scoring run, extending their lead to double-digits five and a half minutes into the game, and never trailed. Within the first ten minutes, Michigan led 23–10, giving Arizona their largest deficit of the season. Lendeborg landed on [[Motiejus Krivas]]' foot, spraining his ankle and [[Medial collateral ligament|MCL]] in the first half. Following his injury, Arizona used an 11–2 run to reduce Michigan's lead to seven points with 7:21 remaining in the half. Michigan then used two 7–0 runs to close the half, leading 48–32 at halftime. Lendeborg returned in the second half and made two three-pointers, followed by two three-pointers by McKenney, giving Michigan a 59–39 lead with 14:35 remaining. From Lendeborg's second three until the 8:38 mark, Michigan made 11-of-13 shot attempts and held an 81–55 lead. Michigan made three field goals in the final seven and a half minutes of the game and Arizona made four field goals while attempting twice as many shots. The Wolverines shot 57.1 percent from the field, including 63.6 percent in the second half. They held Arizona to a season-low 35% field goal percentage for the game. Michigan's 18-point win is tied for the largest between No. 1 seeds in an NCAA men's tournament game since seeding began in [[1979 NCAA Division I basketball tournament|1979]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=401856599 |title=Michigan overpowers Arizona and reaches national title game with 91-73 win |website=[[ESPN.com]] |date=April 4, 2026 |access-date=April 4, 2026}} Michigan became the first team in [[NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] history to score at least 90 points in five consecutive games in a single tournament. They won by double-digits and made at least ten threes in each game.{{cite web|url=https://athlonsports.com/college/michigan-wolverines/basketball/michigan-ncaa-tournament-record-90-points-final-four-arizona |title=Michigan Just Did Something No Team In NCAA Tournament History Has Ever Done |website=athlonsports.com |first=Rodney |last=Knuppel |date=April 4, 2026 |access-date=April 4, 2026}} In fact, no team had ever scored 90+ points five times in a single tournament, consecutive or not.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/michigans-ncaa-tournament-bracket-greatest-march-madness-runs/|title=Michigan's tear through the NCAA Tournament bracket ranks among greatest March Madness runs of all time|access-date=April 8, 2026|date=April 7, 2026|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Nagel, Cody}} ====National Championship==== {{See also|2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball championship game}} On April 6, Michigan defeated 2-seed No. 7 [[2025–26 UConn Huskies men's basketball team|UConn]], 69–63, to win their second national championship and the first since [[1989 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|1989]].{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/48416755/michigan-holds-uconn-win-second-ncaa-hoops-title |title=Michigan holds off UConn, wins second NCAA basketball title |website=[[ESPN.com]] |first=Jeff |last=Borzello |date=April 6, 2026 |access-date=April 6, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/4/6/mens-basketball-wolverines-triumph-over-huskies-to-win-second-national-championship |title=Wolverines Triumph Over Huskies to Win Second National Championship |website=MGoBlue.com |first=Tom |last=Wywrot |date=April 6, 2026|access-date=April 6, 2026}}{{cite web|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/ncaab/2026/04/06/tarris-reed-transfer-uconn-michigan-basketball/89476042007/|title=Why did Tarris Reed transfer from Michigan to UConn? What to know of Huskies star|access-date=April 8, 2026|date=April 6, 2026|work=[[USA Today]]|author=Curtright, Austin}} Michigan was the first team to appear in a national championship game with a starting lineup composed entirely of transfers.{{cite web|url=https://www.cbssports.com/college-basketball/news/michigan-uconn-ncaa-title-masters-unc-michael-malone/|title=Michigan beats UConn for men's NCAA title; who wins the Masters; UNC hires Michael Malone|access-date=April 8, 2026|date=April 7, 2026|publisher=[[CBS Sports]]|author=Brookhouse, Brent}} They were also the first team whose top-four leading scorers during the season were transfers in their first year with the program. The UConn team included former Wolverine transfer, [[Tarris Reed]].{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/mens-college-basketball/news/mullins-family-shifts-longtime-allegiance-from-michigan-to-uconn-for-national-championship-game|title=Mullins family shifts longtime allegiance from Michigan to UConn for national championship game|access-date=April 8, 2026|date=April 6, 2026|publisher=[[NBC Sports]]|agency=[[Associated Press]]}} Michigan was led by Cadeau with 19 points, who was awarded the [[NCAA Division I basketball tournament Most Outstanding Player|NCAA tournament's Most Outstanding Player]]. Mara finished his [[Michigan Wolverines men's basketball statistical leaders#Blocks|single-season program record for blocks]] with 103 and set an additional single-season record with a 66.8% field goal percentage, passing [[Loy Vaught]]'s mark of 66.1% in 1989.{{cite web|url=https://www.sports-reference.com/cbb/schools/michigan/men/leaders-and-records.html |title=Michigan Men's Basketball Leaders & Records |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=April 8, 2026}} He ranked third in NCAA DI in blocks and fourth in field goal percentage.{{cite web|url=https://www.ncaa.com/stats/basketball-men/d1/current/individual/608 |title=NCAA Men's Basketball Individual Statistics (2025–26) |publisher=[[NCAA]] |access-date=April 8, 2026}} Mara joined Cadeau and Johnson Jr. on the [[2026 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament#Final Four all–tournament team|Final Four All-Tournament team]]. Johnson Jr. was a second-team All-Big Ten selection by the media and third team by the coaches, [[Elliot Cadeau]] received an All-Big Ten honorable mention by the media, and [[Trey McKenney]] was selected for the Big Ten All-Freshman team by the coaches (the only selector).{{cite web|url=https://mgoblue.com/news/2026/3/10/mens-basketball-lendeborg-earns-big-ten-player-of-the-year-as-u-m-hauls-15-all-conference-honors|title=Lendeborg Earns Big Ten Player of the Year as U-M Hauls 15 All-Conference Honors|date=March 10, 2026|access-date=March 10, 2026|first=Tom|last=Wywrot|publisher=University of Michigan Athletics}}{{cite web|url=https://bigten.org/mbb/article/59585/|title=Big Ten Announces 2026 Men's Basketball Postseason Honors|date=March 10, 2026|access-date=March 11, 2026|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} Nationally, May was selected as the coach of the year, given the [[Henry Iba Award]] by the [[U.S. Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).
